column1: # Phase 3: supported historical partial order for the audited early cascade.
# Only evidence-backed edges appear. There are deliberately NO blanket
# "all nwgmc before all pwgmc" edges: cohorts are determined by adjudicated
# evidence, not by a predetermined permutation. Rules in the same broad stage
# whose mutual chronology is unknown are left unordered.
#   historical_relative_chronology = a dated ordering supported by lexical
#   fst_dependency        = required by the CAPR implementation (rule feeds/bleeds
#   technical_dependency  = a computational placement requirement (stage != order)
#   historical_stage      = ordering implied purely by secure stage precedence
#       (used sparingly; none asserted here without a concrete witness)
# confidence: A = lexically forced / secure ; B = analysis-dependent ; C = unresolved
# "later" endpoints outside the audited set (SC036, SC040, SC043, SC044, SC051,
# SC052, SC063) are named so Phase 4 can honour the boundary.

column7: evidence
shoulders root vowel: delaying SC005 past SC017 gives the wrong *u; Campbell §331(6); demonstrated dependency
OE nett: *natją>*nattją must geminate before syllabic-j; Ringe&Taylor vol.2 p.50; germanic.txt note
*rástōz>ræste: raising must precede final-*z* loss; reader 020-wgmc-final-z-deletion.md
*bébruz>befer: final-*z* loss precedes medial u-lowering; reader 020
*sáiwalō>sāwol: monophthongization precedes interstress raising; reader 004
terminus ante quem: delaying rhotacism past breaking gives *lirnian/*merde not liornian/meorde; reader 003
fist/goose/youth corridor: vowel effect requires the conditioning nasal present before deletion; change report 026-027
feeding: NWGmc u-lowering *juka>*joka precedes the OE/WS glide spelling geoc (Fulk §4.3 p.56; Campbell §115; Brunner §92.1; R/T p.5, p.129; sc016-017-adjudication.md)
[β] must surface only on singleton *b, so allophony follows gemination; germanic.txt; change report 049-050
SC042 creates the surviving-bimoric ō input that SC043 brightens (rest pathway); change report 042
SC050 is a feeder into the palatalization region; change report 049-050
SC050 feeds velar palatalization; change report 049-050
*-n after *ī loss follows OE high-vowel apocope (cross-source: R/T vol.2 pp.71-72; Campbell §§472-473; Brunner §280; Fulk §7.34; Bammesberger §7.3.4)

Crist: WGmc rhotacism follows earlier WGmc *z-deletion (Crist2001 pp.104-106; Crist2002 §6: deletion is *z-sensitive — *miz deletes but *hēr keeps r — so deletion precedes the *z/*r merger); R&T vol.2 p.87 (rhotacism at the end of the z-loss sequence). Cascade constraint: EAFRhotacism is composed after MonosyllabicFinalZLoss
Dossier A (sc020-dossier-a): root-noun nominative *-z loss is an early morphological class development preceding the general WGmc final-*z deletion; ordering "before Dossier B's rule"
Dossier C (sc020-dossier-c): feeding relationship — the general unstressed final-*z loss (B) precedes the northern stressed-monosyllable loss (C); R&T vol.2 p.87 sequence
Dossier A item 3: consonant-final root-noun *-z loss precedes/bleeds rhotacism (bōc not **bōr); word-final *z never rhotacizes (R&T vol.2 p.87)
Dossier C: stressed-monosyllable final-*z loss precedes rhotacism, "which comes last" in the z-loss sequence (R&T vol.2 p.87; Crist2002 §6)

Corpus witness you: *izwiz > *iwwiz (assimilation) must precede rhotacism, which would give *irwiz, whence OE eow is underivable (R&T vol.2 pp.41-42; Stiles 1985-6; corpus-maturation-01 adjudication §2)
Feeding, lexically forced by you: the *-i of *iwwiz becomes word-final only after final-*z loss; R&T print the sequence with z-loss applied (vol.2 pp.41-42, 44-45; sc098 dossier §3.1)
Bleeding, R&T's own dating argument: OE eow shows no i-umlaut, so the apocope removed the trigger *-i before umlaut (R&T vol.2 pp.57-58; sc098 dossier §3.3)

Corpus witness you: geminate-w vocalization is PWGmc (*fewwar > *feuwar, R&T vol.2 pp.41-42; Fulk §8.3 pp.204-205), so *iww must vocalize to *eoww before degemination; reversed order strands *iw and eow is underivable (031-034 book dossier §4)
Stausland Johnsen 2015 pp.21-22, 29-30: original unstressed *ō first shortens to *o; medial *o then raises to *u. Corpus witness *wúndōdē > wundude; sc021-adjudication.md §9a.
Stausland Johnsen 2015 pp.21-22, 29-30: original unstressed *ō first shortens to *o; final *o then develops to *a. Corpus witness *mḗnōθz > mōnaþ; sc021-adjudication.md §9a.

Stausland Johnsen 2015 pp.21-22 records medial *u in the earliest eighth-century evidence; Campbell §373 dates the u > o tendency to the ninth century. The *wundōdē witness requires the later order; sc021-adjudication.md §9a.

SC100 must resolve shortened final *o before the later ninth-century SC040 u > o tendency; the domains are distinct, but the dated stage contrast is explicit in Stausland Johnsen 2015 pp.21-22 and Campbell §373; sc021-adjudication.md §9a.
